transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-01-15 16:00 UTC | Duration: 49m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jonas (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood Product), Evan (CTO Pegasus), Lina (Head of Cloud), Samir (Partner PM)

Summary: quick sync to align on packaging and listing playbook for Pegasus marketplace offering, clarify VPC/on-prem options, certification checklist, and joint go-to-market artifacts.

Topics: marketplace listing artifacts, reference architecture (VPC vs hosted), packaging (helm/tar/OCI), KMS/HSM & secrets, billing & metering mapping, certification steps, timeline and owners.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, i think we have about 45 minutes, quick intros real quick — we'll go through the integration playbook and then leave time for questions, sound good?
[00:12] Evan: yep, that's great — thanks Maya.
[00:15] Jonas: cool. i'll kick off with the technical scope then we can map to the marketplace checklist.
[00:20] Jonas: so high level, Redwood provides three deployment options: hosted API, dedicated, and private/vpc and for marketplace we commonly list either the hosted integration or provide a bundled deployable for customers who want private. curious which path Pegasus is considering?
[00:34] Lina: we're leaning toward a bundled listing — most of our enterprise customers require VPC or on-prem controls, also need KMS integration and audit logging. we want the listing to show both options if possible.
[00:45] Maya: ok understood. that aligns with other partner listings we've done. bundling is a bit more work but gives you broader coverage in the marketplace. we have a playbook that details artifacts — container image + helm chart, terraform for infra, a sample refarch doc, and a certification checklist. i'll share links after this call.
[01:02] Samir: quick question on billing — will marketplace meter through Pegasus or Redwood billing? we've got to coordinate SKU mapping.
[01:10] Priya: good point. two patterns: 1) listing that proxies Redwood hosted and Pegasus handles marketplace billing as a reseller, or 2) packaged private deployment where Pegasus sells deployment/managed service and metering is handled by your backend. we can give an example mapping sheet.
[01:28] Evan: what's the effort on your side to certify the helm chart for marketplace? our infra team wants to know how long validations take.
[01:35] Jonas: typical validation is CI smoke + functional + marketplace validator (security checks). for the bundle listing we run a sandbox deploy in our lab, run a set of smoke tests and a small benchmark. certification usually takes 1-2 weeks depending on fixes.
[01:49] Lina: do you require SOC2 or is marketplace-level audit enough? some customers ask for SOC2 type II.
[01:55] Maya: Redwood has SOC2 and can provide the security pack; marketplace listing itself also requests audit evidence. if customers require SOC2 we can provide our report and an addendum about data controls. we'll attach those docs.
[02:06] Jonas: also, for customer-managed VPC deployments we expect to validate KMS integration flow: how you manage keys, whether you use an HSM, and the rotation policy. sometimes the transcription picks up weird names — KV cache was mentioned earlier — but that's separate, that's at runtime.
[02:25] Evan: yeah, we will use our KMS — Thales HSM in our env — so we need to confirm Redwood supports BYOK/HSM.
[02:31] Jonas: yes we support BYOK via standard KMS integrations and can document the HSM handshake steps; there may be an ops runbook change.
[02:39] Samir: another integration detail — we need to ensure telemetry flows to Pegasus metrics for billing. you mentioned a metering connector earlier?
[02:47] Maya: correct, we have a marketplace metering connector that can push usage events or you can poll an export. we'll share the mapping doc that ties Redwood usage metrics to marketplace SKU lines.
[03:00] [00:03:00] Lina: ok, packaging specifics: we want an OCI image that we can host in our registry, and a helm chart that supports RBAC, podSecurity, and options for private networking. any blockers?
[03:14] Jonas: that's standard. helm values include networkPolicy, nodeSelector, and a chart value to toggle 'redwood_hosted: true/false' — when false it expects env keys for your KMS/secret manager. we'll include an example values file.
[03:30] Priya: and also we have a 'deployment mode' flag that flips telemetry routing; we'll make sure the chart supports that.
[03:40] Evan: would the redis/kv cache be included in the chart or left as an external dependency?
[03:46] Jonas: usually external, we provide a reference for using managed Redis or stateful sets; caching parameters are configurable. for big workloads we recommend dedicated cache and explicit sizing guidance we will share.
[03:57] [00:04:00] Samir: about the ref arch doc — can you show us the recommended network topology for private deployment? NAT, private subnets, ingress, egress patterns?
[04:09] Jonas: yep, in the refarch we show two patterns: 1) VPC integrated (customer VPC peered to Redwood control plane for telemetry + updates), and 2) fully air-gapped where updates are delivered via an operator bundle and offline artifacts. we'll attach diagrams.
[04:26] Lina: air-gapped is important for a few customers, what does the offline operator path look like?
[04:31] Jonas: you get a signed operator bundle, OCI images, and a verification manifest; deployment is manual but we provide a runbook and a connector for usage reporting if they allow a batched upload.
[04:44] Evan: security checks — do you run static scan and image signing checks as part of the marketplace validator?
[04:50] Maya: yes we require image signing and basic static scanning; for partners we can help onboard to the signing process.
[04:56] [00:05:00] Samir: timeline question — target is a Feb marketplace launch window. is that feasible?
[05:02] Maya: possible but tight. if we get test tenant and SSO info this week and packaging checklist by Monday, SE can run the cert and benchmarks mid-late Jan. final listing cert by early Feb assuming no major fixes.
[05:14] Lina: ok we can aim to have SSO metadata by Jan 22.
[05:19] Priya: one more thing on runtime: we need expected latency targets for the three flavors: hosted, dedicated reserved, and private. customers ask for p95 under 200ms for short prompts.
[05:31] Jonas: we'll produce an estimated table — hosted (p95 ~80-150ms typical for small models), dedicated depends on instance class, private varies with infra. we'll run a Pegasus sample through our harness and share measured numbers.
[05:44] Evan: what about quantization/weight artifact requirements? if we want to host on smaller instances, do you support int8 or other quant modes?
[05:51] Jonas: yes we support quantized model artifacts; packaging needs to indicate quant variant and runtime flags. we'll include a recommended quant profile for cost optimized SKU.
[06:03] [00:06:00] Samir: docs & marketing assets — marketplace listing needs screenshots and short video, can Redwood provide sample video or template?
[06:11] Maya: we have a content pack with screenshots, boilerplate copy, and a 60s explainer video template you can reuse. i'll drop links.
[06:19] Lina: about SSO — we will be SAML-based, can you support SAML metadata upload per tenant?
[06:24] Jonas: yes SAML metadata support is standard for the private deployment flow; hosted flow supports SSO via SSO proxy.
[06:31] [00:07:00] Evan: network egress — what are the IP ranges for Redwood control plane? our security team will need them to allowlist.
[06:38] Maya: we'll provide the IP ranges and also a CIDR recommendation for peering. note that dedicated customers can get static egress by request.
[06:47] Samir: certification checklist items — can we walk through the minimal must-haves?
[06:54] Jonas: sure: 1) container image with digest and signature, 2) helm chart with values schema and schema validation, 3) terraform sample for infra, 4) runbook for KMS/BYOK, 5) smoke tests & benchmark results, 6) security evidence (SAST/DAST basic), 7) license file and legal attestation.
[07:19] Priya: and add monitoring hooks — prometheus metrics or a push endpoint so customers can integrate.
[07:25] Jonas: yes monitoring endpoints and metrics mapping for metering.
[07:29] [00:08:00] Evan: ok great. on certification we might need an enterprise legal checklist — who handles that?
[07:36] Maya: for legal packaging we'll pair with our partner legal ops; i'll introduce someone once we get a formal marketplace listing request.
[07:45] Lina: a small nit — in the helm chart we'd like an option to disable telemetry if a customer is fully air-gapped.
[07:52] Jonas: sure that's our 'telemetry.enabled: false' flag, we'll add a note in the values doc.
[07:57] Samir: one operational question — upgrades and migrations. how are operator upgrades handled across versions?
[08:03] Jonas: we publish semvered operator bundles and we recommend canary upgrades in a staging tenant first; the helm chart supports a 'graceful_migration' option and we provide a migration guide.
[08:15] [00:09:00] Evan: is there any hard dependency on Redwood's control plane for baseline auth and rollout, or can Pegasus choose to fully own control plane?
[08:24] Maya: you can run fully autonomous private with no control plane callbacks for air-gapped setups, but features like live model rollouts and telemetry backfills require a control plane or a batched upload connector.
[08:36] Lina: for compliance we prefer minimal callbacks. can that be limited to outbound only and over a fixed port?
[08:43] Jonas: yes we can restrict outbound endpoints and provide IPs/ports list, the control plane communication is TLS over standard ports.
[08:50] [00:10:00] Samir: ok, let's talk about the joint solution listing copy — we want it to say Pegasus provides managed infra + Redwood inference runtime. do you have a blurb?
[10:06] Maya: yep sample blurb: 'Pegasus Platform and Redwood Inference deliver a turnkey, secure inference solution allowing enterprise teams to run LLM workloads in a customer-controlled environment with predictable latency and cost.' we'll send variations.
[10:24] Evan: fantastic.
[10:28] Priya: i want to call out an edge case — multitenant deployments where Pegasus serves multiple customers from one cluster; we need tenancy isolation guidance.
[10:37] Jonas: in the refarch we include namespace isolation patterns and mTLS options; we recommend per-tenant namespaces + network policies and RBAC.
[10:44] [00:11:00] Lina: testing — for the benchmark can you run both throughput and latency scenarios, and a cost-per-token estimate?
[11:12] Jonas: yes we'll run p50/p95 latency and throughput at a few concurrency points and produce cost estimates by model size and quant profile.
[11:22] Evan: can you also include cold-start behavior notes? that's important for our SLA.
[11:28] Jonas: yep cold start and KV cache warmup will be in the benchmark notes; for sensitive latency SLA we recommend reserved warm pools.
[11:36] [00:12:00] Samir: operational runbooks — want to confirm you have a support SLA for partners during certification window?
[12:03] Maya: yes partner SLA during integration is higher touch; we'll assign an integration SE (that's Jonas) and you'll get priority queuing for any cert blockers.
[12:14] Priya: any special licensing needed to package Redwood runtime with Pegasus distribution?
[12:20] Maya: there is a partner redistribution agreement; i'll loop in partner legal. for the pilot we can do a limited redistribution under a MSA addendum.
[12:32] [00:13:00] Evan: ok good. next steps recap?
[13:00] Maya: quick recap: 1) Redwood shares packaging checklist + helm + terraform samples (owner: Maya) 2) Pegasus provisions test tenant + SSO metadata (owner: Lina) 3) Redwood runs baseline benchmarks and shares latency/cost matrix (owner: Jonas) 4) schedule certification run week of Jan 26.
[13:26] Lina: yes we will aim for those dates.
[13:29] Samir: can we get a short 30-minute follow-up next week to review the checklist?
[13:34] Maya: sure i'll send calendar invite for Jan 20 30-minute follow up.
[13:38] [00:14:00] Evan: thanks everyone, this was helpful.
[13:42] Maya: thanks all, we'll circulate artifacts and next steps. bye.

Action items (reiterated):
- Maya: share packaging checklist + helm chart + terraform module (link placeholder: https://redwood.internal/partners/pegasus/playbook)
- Lina: provide test tenant + SSO metadata by 2026-01-22
- Jonas: run perf harness on sample workload and share p50/p95/throughput/cost by 2026-01-24
